question.text: How many viewers (millions, combined average across channels) will Spain's 26 November 2026 televised leaders' debate draw?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves on the combined average audience ('audiencia media', in millions of viewers) that the televised leaders' debate broadcast on Spanish linear television on 26 November 2026 drew across all channels that aired it. A qualifying debate is one in which candidates for the Presidency of the Government ('cabezas de lista' to Congress) of at least two of the following take part: PSOE (Pedro Sánchez), PP (Alberto Núñez Feijóo), Vox (Santiago Abascal), and the main national left-of-PSOE formation (reported during this campaign as Frente Amplio, with Ada Colau among its leaders); a debate counts whether or not any particular leader attends, and a panel of spokespeople or representatives who are not those candidates does not qualify.

The figure of record is the combined debate audience published by Barlovento Comunicación in its audience publications for 26 November 2026 (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/publicaciones), whether as a dedicated debate analysis or as a combined figure in its daily report for that date. Only if Barlovento publishes no combined figure is the value obtained by adding the debate's per-channel 'audiencia media' listings in that report, counting only channels that aired the debate in full (highlights, excerpts, news items, and delayed or partial broadcasts excluded). The value is expressed in millions of viewers: a debate averaging 5,432,000 viewers across all channels resolves as 5.432.

If no qualifying debate is broadcast on 26 November 2026, the question is annulled; if more than one qualifying debate airs that day, the one with the largest combined average audience is used. If Barlovento publishes no debate figure at all, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The audience counted is that of the debate broadcast itself, not of any surrounding preview, analysis or post-debate programme; where the source distinguishes the debate segment from a longer programme block, the debate-only figure is used. Peak-minute ('minuto de oro') and cumulative-reach ('espectadores únicos') figures are not used. A debate that begins on 26 November 2026 local time counts even if it runs past midnight.

# Research brief: audience for Spain's 26 November 2026 leaders' debate

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: I read Barlovento's Publicaciones page (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/publicaciones) directly, with no summarising. It returned only menu and cookie text. I found no data file behind it and no list of debate analyses. The daily reports are posted under /audiencias-diarias/, for example the 12 Nov report cited in the question. Nothing exists yet for 26 Nov: the figure would come out on the morning of 27 Nov. [Barlovento](https://barloventocomunicacion.es/publicaciones)
- The latest Barlovento data point given in the question is 12 Nov 2026. That day's top programme was Czech Republic-Spain football on La 1, with 4,139,000 viewers and a 30.9% share. Leading news bulletins drew about 2.1-2.3M.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The debate is reported as scheduled but has not taken place.
- 2026-11-14: Sources close to the negotiating teams say the main candidates' debate will be on Thursday 26 Nov. It is organised by the Academia de Televisión, with Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau expected. It will use the same five topic blocks as the cara a cara. The Academia offers a feed that any broadcaster may air. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/11/14/el-debate-entre-los-principales-candidatos-ya-tiene-fecha-se-celebrara-una-semana-despues-del-cara-a-cara/), [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/amp/espana/politica/el-debate-electoral-con-los-cuatro-principales-candidatos-sera-el-jueves-26-tres-dias-antes-de-la-votacion.html)
- Still open: Podemos has asked for Irene Montero to take part. The Academia referred this to the Junta Electoral Central (JEC), which has not ruled. If she is admitted, it becomes a five-way debate. [El Plural](https://www.elplural.com/extratele/debate-cuatro-sera-26-noviembre-podemos-queda-pendiente-junta-electoral_804221102)
- I found no confirmed list of channels for 26 Nov.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

Mediaset (Telecinco/Cuatro) had not confirmed, though it moved the Gran Hermano VIP 9 premiere from Thursday to Wednesday. ## 4. Base rates
Combined averages across channels (Kantar/Barlovento):
- 2015 four-way: 9.23M. 2016 four-way: 10.50M.
- April 2019 four-ways: 8.89M and 9.48M. November 2019 five-way: 8.63M.
- 10 Jul 2023 cara a cara: 5.91M on 2 channels. Vozpópuli called it the least-watched cara a cara in history. [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/medios/cara-a-cara-sanchez-feijoo-menos-visto-historia-espectadores-cuota.html)
- 19 Jul 2023 RTVE three-way: about 4M, without Feijóo, who did not attend.
- Trend: multi-candidate debates fell from about 9-10.5M (2015-2019) to about 4-6M (2023). Total linear TV viewing has kept falling since then.
- Pattern: debates carried by many channels (12 in November 2019) have the highest totals. A debate on one broadcaster group draws less.
- If the absent leader is from a minor party, the drop is small. If a main leader is missing, it is large (2023 three-way).
- This is a one-off event, so seasonality does not apply. Late November is a high-viewing time of year, and Thursday prime time is a normal slot.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on the debate's audience.
- Related market prices on 16 Nov: Polymarket gives PP the win at 0.805 and a PP+Vox majority at 0.88. Kalshi gives Feijóo as next PM at 0.83. These suggest the race is seen as fairly settled, which may dampen interest.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 19 Nov: Sánchez-Feijóo cara a cara. Its figure, out on 20 Nov, is the best calibration point; compare it with 2023's 5.91M. Which channels carry it, especially whether Mediaset does, will likely carry over to 26 Nov.
- JEC ruling on Podemos: decides whether this is a four-way or five-way debate.
- 23 Nov: Atresmedia four-way (whether Sánchez attends) and the RTVE spokespeople debate. Having recently watched a similar debate may reduce interest on 26 Nov.
- Before 26 Nov: final channel list and start time. Check whether Telecinco, Cuatro and the regional channels carry it.
- 27 Nov morning: Barlovento's daily report and any dedicated debate analysis.
- Outcome not driven by weather.

What the history shows:
- The trend is steadily down, from roughly 9-10M in 2015-2019 to 4-6M in 2023.
- Carriage matters a lot. Debates on RTVE alone landed near 4M, while multi-network simulcasts reached 6-9M.
- When a cara a cara came first (2023), the later multi-party debate drew less.
- Season: the 2023 debates were in July, when TV viewing is low. November 2019 (8.6M) is the only debate held in the same season, and overall linear viewing has fallen since then. Total TV viewers on 2026-11-12 were 28.07M, at 170 minutes per person.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- Pending: the JEC ruling on Podemos/Montero joining (a five-way), and whether Telecinco/Mediaset carries the debates.

- Risk: a leader pulling out (Feijóo skipped the 2023 multi-party debate), and the Atresmedia 23 November four-way possibly drawing off some interest.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The debate is scheduled for Thursday 26 November, about 10 days from now. Barlovento's figure should appear on the morning of 27 November, roughly 11 days away.

(b) **Latest known values:** No debate figure exists yet. Barlovento's 12 Nov 2026 report shows the top programme at 4.14M (a football match on La 1) and news bulletins at about 2.1-2.3M. On 13 Nov the laSexta spokespeople four-way drew 1.33M on one channel. Sánchez on El perro andaluz drew 2.85M.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The latest comparable leaders' debates are the 2023 cara a cara (5.91M on 2 channels) and the 2023 RTVE three-way (about 4M on one group). An Academia signal on La 1, Antena 3 and laSexta, plus minor channels, suggests about 5-6M.

(d) **If the trend continued:** Linear TV keeps shrinking, which pulls the figure down. Wider carriage, with RTVE plus Atresmedia and possibly Mediaset, pushes it up. Interest is also high because of the rail crash, the strike and the housing fight. On balance the trend points to about 5-5.5M.

(e) **Historical variation:** Multi-candidate debates ranged from 8.6M to 10.5M in 2015-2019 and from 4M to 6M in 2023. Carriage and attendance account for differences of about ±30-40%. The 19 Nov cara a cara figure will narrow this, but it is not available yet.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There is no market on the audience. Election markets see a PP win as likely (about 80%), which may slightly dampen interest.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Sánchez or Feijóo pulls out, or carriage is limited to RTVE. Fatigue after the Atresmedia four-way on 23 Nov, which might include Sánchez, could also cut the figure. Any of these gives about 2.5-3.5M.
- **High:** Mediaset and the regional channels all carry the signal, and a dramatic campaign closes with a tightening race. That could push the figure to about 8M or more.
